requirements.requirement: Kernel boots with audit=1 on node1
requirements.summary: Post-reboot /proc/cmdline captured in cmd-01ee505330dc4c68 shows 'audit=1' present in the live kernel command line, confirming the running kernel actually booted with the parameter (not just configured).

grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args=audit=1 updated the BLS boot entry file and /etc/default/grub GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX (cmd-1e9d01a7747a4d32), and a full reboot with a changed boot_id (31b01b46... -> 2902703f...) confirmed the parameter was still applied post-restart via both /proc/cmdline and grubby --info=DEFAULT (cmd-01ee505330dc4c68), demonstrating the config-level change survives an actual reboot rather than only a runtime edit.

overall_summary: The task required node1's kernel to boot with audit=1 and retain that setting across reboots. The executor applied audit=1 persistently via grubby (updating both the BLS entry and /etc/default/grub), captured a healthy pre-restart baseline, performed an acknowledged reboot, observed a changed boot_id confirming a real restart, and then directly verified post-reboot that /proc/cmdline contains audit=1, systemd is healthy, and grubby still reports the parameter as default — a full, directly observed healthy-baseline/disruption/recovery transition. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were introduced, and the lifecycle snapshot comparison shows no residue, failed services, or package-health issues beyond expected reboot-related churn.
limitations: Only a single reboot cycle was observed; long-term durability across multiple reboots is inferred from the persisted BLS/grub config rather than repeatedly tested.
auditd service itself was inactive both before and after (not part of the stated task, which only concerns the kernel boot parameter, not the auditd daemon state).

operational_hygiene.summary: Command trace is tight and every state-changing action maps directly to the task: cmd-1e9d01a7747a4d32 applies audit=1 via grubby (the required change), cmd-72d10b928e75430f schedules a transient systemd-run reboot unit used solely to trigger and observe the bounded restart needed to validate persistence, and the rest are read-only inspection/verification commands. The transient antrieb-reboot systemd-run unit is expected to be consumed by the reboot itself and is not retained abnormal residue. Lifecycle diff (after_executor vs before_prepare) shows only expected boot-identity, ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs, and re-bound socket PIDs from the reboot, no failed services, no package-health regression, no unexplained listening sockets or files. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found.
